title: Burns first aid
about: Walks a first aider through calling for help, cooling a burn for 20 minutes and covering it.

sources.name: Hato Hone St John first aid library, Burns

warning: If you have a person in urgent need of medical attention, call 111 now.
audience: Anyone giving first aid for a burn
version: St John web page, read 18 Nov 2026 (no review date shown)

lines.text: Check that the person is happy for you to touch them before you give first aid.

quotes.text: Check that the person is happy for you to touch them before you give first aid

lines.text: If they are unconscious and need lifesaving first aid, don't delay.
Reworded from the same Quick help item; no exact quote captured.
A dry cough can mean smoke or fire has damaged the airway: choose "Smoke or gas".
Reworded from "What to look for"; no exact quote captured.
Electricity is named on the page as a cause, but it gives no separate steps, so there is no answer for it.

options.label: Heat, hot liquid or a hot object
Smoke or gas: burns in the mouth or throat

lines.text: Call 111 for an ambulance if any of these is true:
The burn is larger than half the person's arm.

quotes.text: Call 111 for an ambulance if the area of the burn is larger than half the person’s arm;

lines.text: The burn causes severe pain.
The burn involves the eyes.
Severe pain and eyes are from the same Quick help list; only the "half the person's arm" line was captured word for word.
Call 111 for an ambulance.

quotes.text: Call 111 for an ambulance if the area of the burn is larger than half the person’s arm;

lines.text: Start cooling the burn while you wait.
Call 111 for an ambulance urgently.
Call 111.
Remove contaminated clothing. If the chemical is a powder, brush it off carefully.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured.
Soak the area with lots of water.

quotes.text: Soak the area with lots of water

lines.text: If the eyes are affected, rinse the eyes and under the eyelids with water.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured.
Bitumen: very carefully try to crack the bitumen with scissors, taking care not to damage the skin underneath.

quotes.text: Very carefully try to crack the bitumen with scissors taking care not to damage the skin underneath

lines.text: The page does not say how long to soak a chemical burn. Follow the advice of the 111 call taker.
Gap in the guideline: no soaking time for chemical burns, so this route does not use the 20-minute heat-burn timer.

steps.title: Burns in the mouth or throat

lines.text: The throat, airway and lungs may be damaged. Call 111 urgently.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured for this line.
Move the person to a safe area, preferably outside into fresh air.

quotes.text: Move the person to a safe area, preferably outside into fresh air.

lines.text: Call 111.
If breathing is hard, help them into a position with the head and chest raised.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured.
Deliberate: the page's smoke section has no cooling or covering steps.
Smother the flames with a coat or blanket if you can.
Stop, drop and roll: stop them running or waving their arms, get them to the ground and roll them to put the fire out.
Both lines reworded from the page's "Clothing on fire" section; no exact quote captured.

steps.title: Cool the burn for at least 20 minutes

lines.text: Pour cool water over the burn.

quotes.text: Pour cool water over the burn for at least 20 minutes.

lines.text: Any cool, clean liquid can be used. A hand or foot can go in a bowl or bucket of water.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured.
Remove tight clothing or jewellery near the burn (it may swell), and clothing splashed with hot liquid or chemicals.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured.
Cool the burn, not the child. Do not put small children or babies into a cold bath or shower for a full 20 minutes.

quotes.text: Put small children or babies into a cold bath or shower for a full 20 minutes

lines.text: Use cool, not cold, water.

quotes.text: Remember to cool the burn not the child, so use cool (NOT cold) water.

lines.text: The quote sits under the page's "DO NOT" heading; the app adds "Do not" so the meaning is kept (lessons trap 10).
Don't break blisters, remove anything stuck to the burn, or put creams or lotions on it.
From the page's "DO NOT" list, reworded; no exact quote captured.
The timer shows the minimum. The page says "at least" 20 minutes and gives no upper limit.
Lessons trap 6: "at least 20 minutes" sets a minimum only. The page does not say what to do if 20 minutes of cooling is not possible.

ask.question: Has the burn been cooled for at least 20 minutes?

options.label: It can't be cooled for 20 minutes

lines.text: The page does not say what to do if the burn can't be cooled for 20 minutes.
Call 111 for advice if you are unsure.
Gap in the guideline (lessons trap 13). Advice to call 111 rests on the page's closing line.

quotes.text: If you have a person in urgent need of medical attention, call 111 now.

lines.text: Cover the burn with a non-adhesive dressing or loose cling film.

quotes.text: Cover the burn by using a non-adhesive dressing or loose cling film.

lines.text: Don't use cling film on the face.

quotes.text: Don’t use cling film on the face.

lines.text: Use a sterile dressing if you have one, or wrap cling film or a plastic bag loosely around it. Don't use a sticky dressing: it can harm the skin around the burn.
Reworded from the page; no exact quote captured.
